service.summary: Eligible Ipswich households can order a FLEXiSKiP bag and arrange collection when it suits them instead of waiting for a suburb-wide date.
service.frequency: One free service is available to each eligible household per year.
service.allowance: The service uses a 2 cubic metre FLEXiSKiP bag with a total weight limit of 165 kilograms.
service.eligibility: Most residents with a wheelie-bin collection and at least 4 metres of unobstructed kerb access are eligible. Some unit complexes, rural properties and inaccessible sites are excluded.
service.timing: Council says bag delivery takes up to 10 business days. The bag must be filled and collection booked within 21 days, with collection generally taking 1 to 10 business days.
service.items: The official list includes furniture, mattresses, appliances, carpet, some timber, garden organics and selected masonry. Hazardous waste, food waste, batteries, tyres and broken glass are excluded.
service.notice: From September 2026, Council says eligible residents will choose either the large-item kerbside service or an annual waste voucher. Check the official page for the current arrangement.

service.shortLabel: Up to six bookings a year
service.summary: Most Central Coast households can book general or green bulk waste collections rather than waiting for a fixed suburb-wide date.
service.frequency: Residents of most households can book up to six general or green waste bulk kerbside collections each year.
service.allowance: Each allocation is up to 2 cubic metres, roughly one box-trailer load.
service.eligibility: The service is available to most households, but the property address and remaining allocations must be confirmed in the official booking system.
service.timing: Book before putting anything out, then place accepted items at the kerb on the night before the confirmed collection day.
service.items: General bulk waste and bulk vegetation are accepted under separate guidelines and must be presented as separate piles. Check the official guidelines for item and size restrictions.

service.shortLabel: Up to twelve bookings a year
service.summary: Blacktown City residents can request a household clean-up date online instead of waiting for a scheduled suburb-wide collection.
service.frequency: Eligible residents can book up to 12 household clean-up collections a year with no extra fee.
service.allowance: Each collection is limited to one box-trailer load, stated by Council as 2 metres by 1 metre by 1 metre.
service.eligibility: The property must pay for a Council waste service and the person booking must live at the property. Strata and real-estate managers cannot book on a resident's behalf.
service.timing: Council advises planning ahead because the next available date may be up to four weeks away. Items must not be placed out before the night preceding the confirmed date.
service.items: Furniture, mattresses, whitegoods, carpet and bundled garden material are among the accepted items. Building waste, hazardous materials, vehicle parts, glass and overly heavy items are excluded.

service.summary: Newcastle residents can request a kerbside bulk-waste pickup or use a self-haul voucher instead of waiting for a neighbourhood collection.
service.frequency: Residents can request two services—two pickups, two vouchers or one of each—within a rolling 12-month period.
service.allowance: Each service covers up to 2 cubic metres of bulk waste, roughly a 6-by-4-foot box trailer loaded one metre high.
service.eligibility: Only people who live at the property can request the service. The official request flow confirms the address, entitlement and current waiting time.
service.timing: Kerbside pickup waiting times vary with demand in each suburb. Council describes the digital self-haul voucher as the quickest option.
service.items: Both options accept many bulky household items; self-haul vouchers accept a wider range. The official guide distinguishes kerbside items from material that must go to Summerhill.
